at opstå.explanation: "At opstå" means "to arise / occur". To say a problem or event comes into being, use it with the thing that appears: "Der opstod en brand" (A fire broke out). To say you get out of bed, use "at stå op" (to get up): "Jeg står op klokken syv" (I get up at seven).

at opsummere.explanation: "At opsummere" means "to summarize". To start giving the key points at the end of a meeting, say: "Lad mig lige opsummere" (Let me sum it up quickly). The noun for the result is "en opsummering" (a summary).

at opsætte.explanation: "At opsætte" means "to set up". It is built from "op" (up) and "at sætte" (to put). To say you set up a shelf, say: "Jeg opsætter en hylde" (I am setting up a shelf). To make an account or a company, use "at oprette" (to create): "Jeg opretter en konto" (I create an account).

at opsøge.explanation: "At opsøge" means "to seek out". It is built from "op" (up) and "at søge" (to search). To say you go to a person on purpose, use it with the person: "Han opsøgte lægen" (He went to see the doctor).

at optage.explanation: "At optage" means "to record", as in saving sound or video. To say you record a song, use it with the thing you save: "Jeg optager sangen" (I am recording the song). When you talk about something that fills room, it means "to take up": "Det optager meget plads" (It takes up a lot of space).

at optimere.explanation: "At optimere" means "to optimize". To say you make something work as well as possible, use it with the thing: "Vi optimerer ruten" (We optimize the route). To say only that something becomes better, use "at forbedre" (to improve): "Jeg forbedrer min dansk" (I am improving my Danish).

at optrappe.explanation: "At optrappe" means "to escalate". It is built from "op" (up) and "en trappe" (a staircase). To say you increase the effort step by step, use it with the thing that grows: "Vi optrapper indsatsen" (We are stepping up the effort).

at optræde.explanation: "At optræde" means "to perform / appear". When you talk about someone on stage, it means "to perform": "Bandet optræder i aften" (The band is performing tonight). When you talk about taking a role, it means "to appear": "at optræde som vidne" (to appear as a witness).

at ordne.explanation: "At ordne" means "to fix / sort out". To promise you will take care of a task yourself, say: "Jeg ordner det" (I will sort it out). To say a problem will work out, use "sig" (itself): "Det ordner sig" (It will work out).

at organisere.explanation: "At organisere" means "to organize". To say you plan and arrange an event, use it with the event: "Hun organiserer en tur" (She is organizing a trip). To say you put things in order, use it with the things: "Jeg organiserer mine filer" (I am organizing my files).

at orientere.explanation: "At orientere" means "to inform / orient". To say you tell people about something, add "om" (about): "Direktøren orienterer medarbejderne om planerne" (The director informs the staff about the plans). To say you look around to get your bearings, add "sig" (oneself): "Jeg orienterer mig på kortet" (I get my bearings on the map).

at orke.explanation: "At orke" means "to have the energy for". To say you cannot take any more, add "ikke" (not): "Jeg orker ikke mere" (I can't take any more). To ask whether someone has the energy for something, say: "Orker du at gå en tur?" (Do you have the energy for a walk?)

at overbevise.explanation: "At overbevise" means "to convince". To say you make someone believe something by giving reasons, say: "Hun overbeviste mig om, at det var sikkert" (She convinced me that it was safe). To say you get someone to do something, use "at overtale" (to persuade): "Hun overtalte mig til at tage med" (She persuaded me to come along).

at overdrage.explanation: "At overdrage" means "to hand over / transfer". To say something official passes to another person, such as a company or a role, say: "overdrage ledelsen" (to hand over the management). To give someone an ordinary thing, use "at give" (to give): "Jeg giver dig bogen" (I give you the book).

at overdrive.explanation: "At overdrive" means "to exaggerate". To tell someone they are exaggerating, say: "Du overdriver, det var kun to minutter" (You are exaggerating, it was only two minutes). The noun is "en overdrivelse" (an exaggeration): "Det er en overdrivelse" (That is an exaggeration).

at overføre.explanation: "At overføre" means "to transfer". To say you move something from one place or person to another, say: "Jeg overfører penge til din konto" (I transfer money to your account). To say an illness is passed on, say: "at overføre smitte" (to pass on an infection).

at overføre penge.explanation: "At overføre penge" means "to transfer money". To say how often you do it, say: "Hun overfører penge hver måned" (She transfers money every month). To say you send money to a person, use "at sende penge" (to send money): "Jeg sender dig penge" (I send you money).

at overgive sig.explanation: "At overgive sig" means "to surrender". When you say who surrenders, "sig" (oneself) changes with the person: "jeg overgiver mig" (I surrender), "de overgiver sig" (they surrender). To say you give up in a game or an argument, say: "Jeg overgiver mig!" (I give up!)

at overgå.explanation: "At overgå" means "to exceed / surpass". It is built from "over" (over) and "at gå" (to go). To say something turned out better than people hoped, say: "overgå forventningerne" (to exceed the expectations).

at overholde.explanation: "At overholde" means "to comply with". It is built from "over" (over) and "at holde" (to hold). To say you meet a deadline, say: "overholde fristen" (to meet the deadline).

at overkomme.explanation: "At overkomme" means "to manage". To say you do not have the strength or time for a big task, add "ikke" (not): "Jeg kan ikke overkomme det hele" (I cannot manage it all). To say you beat a fear, use "at overvinde" (to overcome): "Hun overvandt sin frygt" (She overcame her fear).

at overlade.explanation: "At overlade" means "to leave (to someone) / hand over". To say you let another person decide, say: "Jeg overlader beslutningen til dig" (I leave the decision to you). To say you leave something to chance, use "til" (to): "overlade noget til tilfældighederne" (to leave something to chance).

at overleve.explanation: "At overleve" means "to survive". It is built from "over" (over) and "at leve" (to live), so it means to live through something. To say someone came through an accident, say: "Han overlevede ulykken" (He survived the accident).

at overnatte.explanation: "At overnatte" means "to stay overnight". It is built from "over" (over) and "en nat" (a night). To say you sleep at a friend's home, say: "Jeg overnatter hos en ven" (I am staying overnight at a friend's).

at overhale.explanation: "At overhale" means "to overtake". To say you pass a vehicle on the road, use it with the vehicle: "Hun overhaler en traktor" (She overtakes a tractor). To say you catch up with someone ahead of you, use "at indhente" (to catch up): "Jeg indhenter dig" (I catch up with you).

at overraske.explanation: "At overraske" means "to surprise". To say you plan something nice for someone, say: "Jeg vil overraske min mor" (I want to surprise my mom). To say something catches people off guard, say: "Regnen overraskede os" (The rain surprised us).

at overrække.explanation: "At overrække" means "to hand over / present". It is built from "over" (over) and "at række" (to pass). To say a prize is handed to someone, say: "Borgmesteren overrakte prisen" (The mayor presented the prize). To ask someone to pass you something at the table, use "at række": "Kan du række mig saltet?" (Can you pass me the salt?)

at overse.explanation: "At overse" means "to overlook". To say you miss something by accident, say: "Jeg overså fejlen" (I missed the error). To say you choose not to react to something small, say: "Jeg overser det denne gang" (I will let it pass this time).

at overskride.explanation: "At overskride" means "to exceed". To say you go past a limit, use it with the limit: "Vi har overskredet budgettet" (We have gone over the budget). To say you keep to a limit, use "at overholde" (to comply with): "Jeg overholder fartgrænsen" (I keep to the speed limit).

at overskue.explanation: "At overskue" means "to get an overview of". To say something is too much for you, add "ikke" (not): "Jeg kan ikke overskue det" (It is too much for me). To say you can see the whole situation, say: "Jeg kan overskue situationen" (I can get an overview of the situation).

at oversætte.explanation: "At oversætte" means "to translate". To say you translate a text, use it with the text: "Jeg oversætter brevet" (I translate the letter). To name the languages, use "fra" (from) and "til" (to): "Hun oversætter fra dansk til tysk" (She translates from Danish to German).

at overtage.explanation: "At overtage" means "to take over". To ask someone to take your place, say: "Kan du overtage rattet?" (Can you take over the wheel?) To say you accept a duty, say: "at overtage ansvaret" (to take over the responsibility).

at overtale.explanation: "At overtale" means "to persuade". To say you get someone to say yes, say: "Hun overtalte mig til at komme med" (She persuaded me to come along). To say you change what someone believes, use "at overbevise" (to convince): "Han overbeviste mig om, at det var sandt" (He convinced me that it was true).

at overtræde.explanation: "At overtræde" means "to violate". To say you break a rule or a limit, use it with the rule: "overtræde fartgrænsen" (to break the speed limit). To say you follow a rule, use "at overholde" (to comply with): "Jeg overholder reglerne" (I follow the rules).

at overveje.explanation: "At overveje" means "to consider". To say you think about something carefully before you decide, say: "Jeg overvejer at flytte" (I am considering moving). To say what is on your mind, use "at tænke" (to think): "Jeg tænker på mad" (I am thinking about food).

at overvinde.explanation: "At overvinde" means "to overcome". To say you get past something difficult, say: "Vi overvandt problemerne" (We overcame the problems). To say you win a game, use "at vinde" (to win): "Vi vandt kampen" (We won the match).

at overvåge.explanation: "At overvåge" means "to monitor / watch". To say people follow a patient over time, say: "Lægerne overvåger patienten" (The doctors are monitoring the patient). To say you follow something such as prices, say: "Hun overvåger priserne" (She monitors the prices).

en oberst.explanation: "En oberst" means "a colonel". To say which part of the armed forces someone serves in, say: "Han er oberst i hæren" (He is a colonel in the army).

en odder.explanation: "En odder" means "an otter". Wild otters live in Denmark.

en officer.explanation: "En officer" means "an officer", as in the armed forces. To say a police officer, use "en betjent" (a police officer): "Betjenten stoppede bilen" (The police officer stopped the car).

en offside.explanation: "En offside" means "an offside". To say the referee calls it, say: "Dommeren dømte offside" (The referee called offside).

en okse.explanation: "En okse" means "an ox". The part "okse" also appears in "oksesteg" (roast beef).

en oldefar.explanation: "En oldefar" means "a great-grandfather". It is built from "olde" (one generation further back) and "far" (father). The part "olde" also appears in "et oldebarn" (a great-grandchild). To say someone has one, say: "Hun har et oldebarn" (She has a great-grandchild).

en oldemor.explanation: "En oldemor" means "a great-grandmother". It is built from "olde" (one generation further back) and "mor" (mother). The part "olde" also appears in "et oldebarn" (a great-grandchild). To say someone has one, say: "Hun har et oldebarn" (She has a great-grandchild).

en oliven.explanation: "En oliven" means "an olive". It is the first part of "olivenolie" (olive oil). To say you cook with the oil, say: "Jeg steger i olivenolie" (I fry in olive oil).

en ombudsmand.explanation: "En ombudsmand" means "an ombudsman". It is built from "et ombud" (a representative) and "en mand" (a man). In Denmark, "Folketingets Ombudsmand" (the Parliamentary Ombudsman) looks into complaints about how the state treats people.

en ombygning.explanation: "En ombygning" means "a remodel". The part "om-" means "over again", as in "at omskrive" (to rewrite): "Jeg omskriver teksten" (I am rewriting the text). To say the work is going on right now, say: "Huset er under ombygning" (The house is being remodeled).

en ombytning.explanation: "En ombytning" means "an exchange". It comes from "at bytte om" (to switch around). To say you switch two things around, say: "Vi bytter om på stolene" (We switch the chairs around).

en omgang.explanation: "En omgang" means "a round / lap". To say you buy drinks for a group, say: "Jeg giver en omgang" (I am buying a round). To say you run once around a track, say: "Jeg løber en omgang" (I run one lap).

en omgangskreds.explanation: "En omgangskreds" means "a circle of friends". It is built from "at omgås" (to spend time with) and "en kreds" (a circle). To say how many people you spend time with, say: "Hun har en stor omgangskreds" (She has a large circle of friends).

en omkamp.explanation: "En omkamp" means "a rematch". It is built from "om" (again) and "en kamp" (a match). The part "om" also means "again" in "at lave om" (to redo): "Jeg laver opgaven om" (I redo the assignment).

en omkostning.explanation: "En omkostning" means "a cost". To talk about the costs of running something in the plural, say: "høje omkostninger" (high costs). To ask what one thing you buy costs, use "en pris" (a price): "Hvad er prisen?" (What is the price?)

en omkørsel.explanation: "En omkørsel" means "a detour". To tell someone to follow the route set up around a closed road, say: "Følg omkørslen" (Follow the detour). To say you choose a longer way yourself, use "en omvej" (a longer way): "Jeg tager en omvej hjem" (I take a longer way home).

en omlægning.explanation: "En omlægning" means "a restructuring". It comes from "at lægge om" (to change over): "Hun lægger kosten om" (She changes her diet). To say a loan gets new terms, say: "omlægning af lån" (switching a loan to new terms).

en omstilling.explanation: "En omstilling" means "an adjustment / a transition". To say a change takes getting used to, say: "en stor omstilling" (a big adjustment). To say you call a company, use "omstillingen" (the switchboard): "Jeg ringer til omstillingen" (I am calling the switchboard).

en omstændighed.explanation: "En omstændighed" means "a circumstance". To say you will do something whatever happens, say: "Jeg kommer under alle omstændigheder" (I will come in any case). To say how things are right now, say: "Under de omstændigheder" (Under the circumstances).

en omsætning.explanation: "En omsætning" means "a turnover / revenue". To say what a business has left after costs, use "en fortjeneste" (a profit): "Vi har en stor fortjeneste" (We have a large profit).

en omvej.explanation: "En omvej" means "a detour". To say you take a longer way, say: "Jeg tager en omvej" (I take a longer way). To say you take the shorter way, use "en genvej" (a shortcut): "Jeg tager en genvej" (I take a shortcut).

en onkel.explanation: "En onkel" means "an uncle". To use it as a title before a name, say: "onkel Peter" (Uncle Peter). Danish has separate words for an uncle on each side: "en morbror" (mother's brother) and "en farbror" (father's brother). To say where your father's brother lives, say: "Min farbror bor i Odense" (My father's brother lives in Odense).

en opdagelse.explanation: "En opdagelse" means "a discovery". To say someone found something that was already there, say: "Han gjorde en vigtig opdagelse" (He made an important discovery). To say a person made something new, use "en opfindelse" (an invention): "Hjulet er en gammel opfindelse" (The wheel is an old invention).

en opdatering.explanation: "En opdatering" means "an update". The verb is "at opdatere" (to update): "Jeg opdaterer appen" (I am updating the app).

en opdeling.explanation: "En opdeling" means "a division". It comes from "at dele op" (to split up): "Vi deler klassen op" (We split the class up).

en opdragelse.explanation: "En opdragelse" means "an upbringing". To describe how strict it was, say: "en streng opdragelse" (a strict upbringing). To talk about the years of growing up in a place, use "en opvækst" (an upbringing in a place): "en opvækst på landet" (growing up in the countryside).

en opera.explanation: "En opera" means "an opera". To say you go to the building, say: "Vi skal i operaen i aften" (We are going to the opera tonight). In Copenhagen, "Operaen" (the Opera House) is on the island of Holmen. To say you go to a play, use "et teater" (a theater): "Vi skal i teatret i aften" (We are going to the theater tonight).

en operation.explanation: "En operation" means "an operation", as in surgery at a hospital. The verb is "at operere" (to operate): "Lægen opererer hende" (The doctor is operating on her).

en opfattelse.explanation: "En opfattelse" means "a perception / view". To say what you think about a plan, say: "Min opfattelse er, at planen er for dyr" (My view is that the plan is too expensive). To ask what someone else thinks, say: "Hvad er din opfattelse?" (What is your view?)

en opfindelse.explanation: "En opfindelse" means "an invention". To say something was made long ago, say: "Hjulet er en gammel opfindelse" (The wheel is an old invention). To say someone found something that was already there, use "en opdagelse" (a discovery): "Han gjorde en vigtig opdagelse" (He made an important discovery).

en opfinder.explanation: "En opfinder" means "an inventor". It comes from "at opfinde" (to invent), and "-er" makes it the person who does it, just like in "en lærer" (a teacher). To say what someone is, say: "Hun er opfinder" (She is an inventor).

en opfordring.explanation: "En opfordring" means "a call / appeal". To say someone did something because they were asked, say: "Han sang på opfordring" (He sang when asked to).

en opførelse.explanation: "En opførelse" means "a construction / a performance". To say a big structure is built, use the first meaning: "opførelsen af en bro" (the construction of a bridge). To say a play is shown, use the second meaning: "opførelsen af en opera" (the performance of an opera). To say how someone behaves, use "en opførsel" (behavior): "Hans opførsel var uhøflig" (His behavior was rude).

en opgang.explanation: "En opgang" means "a stairwell / entrance". To say which entrance of an apartment block you live in, say: "Jeg bor i opgang B" (I live in stairwell B).

en opgave.explanation: "En opgave" means "a task". To say what you have to do at school, use it for an exercise: "en matematikopgave" (a math exercise). To say what you are asked to do at work, use it for a duty: "Jeg har en ny opgave" (I have a new task).

en opgavebog.explanation: "En opgavebog" means "an exercise book". It is built from "en opgave" (a task) and "en bog" (a book). To say you write the answers in it, say: "Jeg skriver i opgavebogen" (I am writing in the exercise book).

en opgivelse.explanation: "En opgivelse" means "a giving up". It comes from "at opgive" (to give up): "Han opgav drømmen" (He gave up the dream).

en opgørelse.explanation: "En opgørelse" means "a statement / a count". It comes from "at opgøre" (to work out): "Jeg opgør udgifterne" (I work out the expenses).

en opholdstilladelse.explanation: "En opholdstilladelse" means "a residence permit". It is built from "et ophold" (a stay) and "en tilladelse" (a permission), so it is literally "stay permission". To say you ask the authorities for one, say: "Jeg søger om opholdstilladelse" (I am applying for a residence permit).

en ophævelse.explanation: "En ophævelse" means "an abolition / a cancellation". It comes from "at ophæve" (to repeal). To say a contract is ended officially, say: "ophævelse af kontrakten" (the cancellation of the contract).

en oplader.explanation: "En oplader" means "a charger". The verb is "at oplade" (to charge): "Jeg oplader telefonen" (I am charging the phone).

en oplevelse.explanation: "En oplevelse" means "an experience", as in something you live through. To say an event stayed with you, say: "en uforglemmelig oplevelse" (an unforgettable experience). To talk about work experience or skills, use "erfaring" (experience): "Jeg har ti års erfaring" (I have ten years of experience).

en oplysning.explanation: "En oplysning" means "a piece of information". On a form, the plural "oplysninger" (details) is what you fill in: "Skriv dine oplysninger her" (Write your details here).

en opmuntring.explanation: "En opmuntring" means "an encouragement". To thank someone for cheering you up, say: "Tak for opmuntringen" (Thanks for the encouragement). To call a small gift that cheers someone up, say: "en lille opmuntring" (a little pick-me-up).

en opposition.explanation: "En opposition" means "an opposition". To say someone belongs to the parties outside the government, say: "Han er i oppositionen" (He is in the opposition). To say many people strongly object, say: "Der er stærk opposition mod planen" (There is strong opposition to the plan).

en oprindelse.explanation: "En oprindelse" means "an origin". To ask where a word comes from, say: "Hvad er ordets oprindelse?" (What is the origin of the word?) The adjective is "oprindelig" (original): "den oprindelige plan" (the original plan).

en opringning.explanation: "En opringning" means "a phone call". It is built from "at ringe op" (literally, to ring up): "Jeg ringer dig op i aften" (I will call you tonight). The shorter word "et opkald" (a call) also exists.

en oprydning.explanation: "En oprydning" means "a tidying up". To say it is time to put a room in order, say: "Så er det tid til oprydning" (Now it is time to tidy up). To say you clear up after a storm, say: "oprydning efter stormen" (cleanup after the storm).

en opsang.explanation: "En opsang" means "a telling-off". To say you get one, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik en opsang" (I got told off).

en opsigelse.explanation: "En opsigelse" means "a resignation / notice of termination". To say you end your own job, say: "Jeg afleverer min opsigelse" (I hand in my resignation). To say your employer ends it, say: "at få en opsigelse" (to be let go).

en opskrift.explanation: "En opskrift" means "a recipe". To name the dish, add "på" (for): "en opskrift på pandekager" (a recipe for pancakes). To ask someone to share it, say: "Kan jeg få opskriften?" (Can I have the recipe?)

en opslagstavle.explanation: "En opslagstavle" means "a bulletin board". It is built from "et opslag" (a notice) and "en tavle" (a board). To say you pin a note on it, say: "Jeg satte sedlen op på opslagstavlen" (I pinned the note on the bulletin board).

en opsparing.explanation: "En opsparing" means "savings". To say you put money aside for a goal, use "at spare op" (to save up): "Jeg sparer op til en rejse" (I am saving up for a trip).

en optagelse.explanation: "En optagelse" means "a recording". It comes from "at optage" (to record). To say a person is accepted into a school, use the meaning "admission": "optagelse på universitetet" (admission to the university).

en optiker.explanation: "En optiker" means "an optician". To say you go to see an eye doctor, use "en øjenlæge" (an eye doctor): "Jeg skal til øjenlægen" (I am going to the eye doctor).

en optikerforretning.explanation: "En optikerforretning" means "an optician's shop". It is built from "en optiker" (an optician) and "en forretning" (a shop). To ask for directions, say: "Hvor ligger optikerforretningen?" (Where is the optician's shop?)

en optræden.explanation: "En optræden" means "a performance". To say someone performs for an audience, say: "Hun har en optræden i aften" (She has a performance tonight). To say how someone comes across, say: "Hendes optræden var rolig og sikker" (She came across as calm and confident).

en optælling.explanation: "En optælling" means "a count". It comes from "at tælle op" (to count up). To say how long the counting takes, say: "Optællingen tager en time" (The count takes an hour).

en opvarmning.explanation: "En opvarmning" means "a warm-up". To say players prepare before a match, say: "Spillerne laver en opvarmning" (The players do a warm-up). To talk about heating a building, say: "opvarmning af huset" (heating the house).

en opvask.explanation: "En opvask" means "dishwashing". It comes from "at vaske op" (to wash up). The part "opvask" also appears in "en opvaskemaskine" (a dishwasher): "Jeg tømmer opvaskemaskinen" (I empty the dishwasher).

en opvaskebørste.explanation: "En opvaskebørste" means "a dish brush". It is built from "opvask" (dishes) and "en børste" (a brush). To say what to scrub with it, say: "Brug opvaskebørsten til gryden" (Use the dish brush for the pot).

en opvaskemaskine.explanation: "En opvaskemaskine" means "a dishwasher", as in the machine. To say you empty the machine, say: "Jeg tømmer opvaskemaskinen" (I empty the dishwasher). To say a person who washes dishes, use "en opvasker" (a person who washes dishes): "Han arbejder som opvasker" (He works as a dishwasher).

en opvasker.explanation: "En opvasker" means "a dishwasher", as in a person. To say what someone does for work, say: "Han arbejder som opvasker" (He works as a dishwasher). To say the machine, use "en opvaskemaskine" (a dishwashing machine): "Jeg tømmer opvaskemaskinen" (I empty the dishwasher).
